TIL: If you sleep six hours a night for twelve days, your cognitive and physical performance becomes indistinguishable from that of someone who has been awake for twenty-four hours straight.

I'd like to disagree with this. First, I'll admit I'm reading your title and not the article. Some people are quite happy with six hour sleep cycles. I've found that personally 8 hours makes me groggy, but with 6 I wake almost fully alert and recharged. Some people genetically can do 6. There are also some people that sleep in very odd cycles, giving them far more wake time than the average person.

I noticed as well that it seems easier for me to wake up after 5 hours of sleep than 7. However, after keeping this up for a while I can tell that I was really not functioning better when I regularly slept 5 hours instead of 7. And now, a few years after that "experiment", I tend to think that if I felt groggy after 7 hours of sleep, it's probably because I actually need at least 8 full hours to feel rested.

More research is needed into HOW people wake up as well. Some think that feeling groggy means they overslept while some think it means they didn't sleep enough. We are still learning how the body uses sleep to purify chemicals in the brain and how REM sleep really works.

Personally if I wake naturally I feel great even after only five hours of sleep. If I'm woken by my asshole cat sitting on my face after seven hours of sleep I might feel agitated and groggy.

Humans are so complex.
I've found what works best for me is to sleep 6 hours on most nights and then on the weekends take the opportunity to get a nice 12 hour or so sleep in to catch up on "lost" sleep.
I've been getting 5-6 hours of sleep for years now and I feel amazing. I don't use alarms. My body won't let me sleep any longer than that.

My optimal amount of sleep is 6-8 hours, but I find that if I sleep twice in a day (once in the evening and once in the morning) with a 2-3 hour gap in between, then i'm fine with less than 6 total.

I also feel tired with more than 8.

As someone who is lucky to sleep six hours a night and I am very happy when I do... This is not the case for me.

I know that it is likely that having so little sleep for so long has left me with a high sleep deficit. However, in the occasions that I stay awake for 24 hours straight I turn into a zombie. Slow, cranky, physically and mentally exhausted.
